title: Estimating Atlantic Salmon (Salmo salar) Smolt Outmigration Timing: A Method Comparison
content:
ABSTRACT

Estimates of outmigration timing of Atlantic salmon smolt (Salmo salar) have become crucial inputs for predictive models that quantify effects of anthropogenic impacts. Recent reviews indicate that choice of method may impact estimates of migration timing, demanding an evaluation of the various monitoring tools in tandem. Here, we compared the migration behavior of smolts tagged with PIT tags or acoustic telemetry tags with smolts monitored with river transects of underwater video systems in two rivers in western Norway for three consecutive migration seasons (2019–2021). Despite discrepancies in the quantiles of migration, the methods often observed many of the same local peaks in migration distributions. Choice of tagging location had the largest observed effect on the migration timing of tagged individuals, with smolts from upstream of lakes arriving to the fjord 13.4 days later on average. Smolt length and morphological smolt index had negligible effects on migration timing.
